content: Although the aforementioned methods aim to reduce the domain discrepancy, they do not explicitly minimize the distance between distributions, and some of them highly rely on the selection of pivot features. In our method, we formally construct an objective for this purpose. Similar ideas have been explored in many computer vision problems, where the representations of the underlying domains are encouraged to be similar through explicit objectives BIBREF9 , BIBREF10 , BIBREF11 , BIBREF12 , BIBREF13 such as maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) BIBREF14 . In NLP tasks, Li et al. ( BIBREF15 ) and Chen et al. ( BIBREF16 ) both proposed using adversarial training framework for reducing domain difference. In their model, a sub-network is added as a domain discriminator while deep features are learned to confuse the discriminator. The feature adaptation component in our model shares similar intuition with MMD and adversary training. We will show a detailed comparison with them in our experiments.
